summary: Master MNCH programme management in 5 days. Design results frameworks, use DHIS2 dashboards, and apply WHO standards. Enrol at TrainingCred.com.
lede: MNCH programme management brings situation analysis, planning, implementation and performance review together across maternal, newborn and child health services. Designed for mid-career professionals who manage or support these programmes, the training addresses the task of turning service and coverage data into coordinated programme action. Participants practise assessing coverage with DHS, MICS and SARA data, building results frameworks and theories of change, and using DHIS2 dashboards to review indicators and guide programme improvements.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for mid-career professionals who hold operational or advisory responsibility for MNCH programmes at national, sub-national, district, or facility level, or who support MNCH programme delivery through technical assistance, monitoring, or donor coordination roles.
modules: MNCH Global Landscape and Health System Context
MNCH Situation Analysis and Coverage Assessment
Quality of Care Improvement in MNCH Services
MNCH Monitoring, Data Use, and DHIS2 Dashboards
Community Engagement and Demand Generation for MNCH
MNCH Operational Planning, Costing, and Scale-Up
prerequisites: This is an intermediate-level course. Participants are expected to have at least two years of practical experience in health programme management, public health, or a related field. Prior exposure to MNCH service delivery, reproductive health programming, or health system strengthening is strongly recommended. Familiarity with basic monitoring and evaluation concepts — such as log frames, indicators, and data collection methods — is assumed. No advanced statistical or coding skills are required. Participants should bring a laptop for DHIS2 dashboard exercises; a browser-based DHIS2 demo environment will be provided. Participants are encouraged to bring their own programme documents (log frames, work plans, or indicator tracking sheets) to apply course tools directly to their own context.
